1.why: Reset tokens are stored with an accountKey and password replacement only updates that bound account after identity verification.

2.why: A reset token is bound to one accountKey and cannot change any other user's password.

3.why: replacePassword never deletes or invalidates other entries in the sessions map, so prior sessions keep working.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS, but no explicit minimum TLS version is set in code.

5.why: Passwords use argon2id and tokens are SHA-256 hashed for storage, but this is hashing rather than encryption of reset codes/user data.

6.why: No real email is sent; mock delivery returns raw testValue/testIdentityValue in the API response instead of a guarded message.

7.why: identifier/password validators, body size limits, and client textContent usage constrain and escape user-supplied data.

8.why: renderLink only accepts same-origin paths on / with a recovery-test param and rejects protocol-relative or external URLs.

9.why: There are no server email templates that embed user input, so no script/HTML injection path exists there.

10.why: Mock tokens and MFA codes are written to the on-page logs and returned in JSON test fields, exposing them.

11.why: Runtime secrets are hashed, but provision() hardcodes the plaintext initial password Initial!HospitalPassword9 in source.

12.why: provision() creates accounts with the known default password Initial!HospitalPassword9, so default credentials work.

13.why: Login, reset confirmation, identity, and MFA paths lock out after repeated failures (e.g., 5 tries then LOCK_MS).

14.why: Recovery responses add deliveryPath/testValue only when the account exists, which reveals whether the identifier is valid.

15.why: reset tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues (base64url), are long, and are stored under a per-account digest.
